column2: agreed merge:habéis, but the target is a conjugated form; the lemma is haber (cf. teneis -> tener)
agreed merge:podréis, but the target is a conjugated form; the lemma is poder
agreed merge:dínamo, but most forms are the club name Dinamo (488 of ~710); dinamo is also an accepted spelling: merge, keep or drop?
accent-only merge:líquido; check the hidden verb form liquido (liquidar); examples look like líquido
agreed merge:diezmo, but diezmar is a real verb and its forms (diezmar 300, diezmado 219, diezmada 161, diezmando 132) are verb uses: keep the verb?
agreed merge:opaco, but opacar is a real verb with verb forms (opacar 182, opacado 127, opacada 81) next to opaco/opaca
agreed merge:cascada, but forms include cascara/cascaras (360 = cáscara without accent): two words under one broken lemma
agreed merge:jalea, but forms include jaleo/Jaleo (326), a separate real noun: two words under one lemma
agreed merge:morir (muramos, muráis), but Mures (419) is a name: does the name share go with it?
agreed merge:molestar with no examples; could be the adjective molesto (fem.) rather than the verb
agreed merge:suní; the written singular is sunita (people write sunita/sunitas): spelling rule says the form people write
agreed drop because examples are the name Pacifica, but pacificar is a real verb; a real common word stays even if many occurrences are a name
agreed drop (mostly a plant/name), but humanar is a real verb: is the real-word share a minority?
agreed drop as place name, but chontal is also an indigenous people/language (cf. wayuu, purépecha kept)
agreed drop, but grappa is a liqueur name used in Spanish like amaretto (kept in s4-flagged)
agreed keep (ECOWAS); a regional body: famous international body under the institutions rule, or regional like OEA (dropped earlier)?
agreed keep, but Spanish writes rímel (s4-flagged merges rimmel -> rímel): merge:rímel?
